info.name: SMSGlobal
info.description:
SMSGlobal API Postman Collection.

Find your API credentials in the MXT dashboard: [https://mxt.smsglobal.com/integrations](https://mxt.smsglobal.com/integrations) and copy your Master API Key Username and Password.

In MXT you can also create your REST API credentials for using the SMSGlobal REST API.

On the Postman `Environments` tab, set the following environment variables:

`HttpApiUrl` = [https://api.smsglobal.com](https://api.smsglobal.com)

`RestApiUrl` = [https://api.smsglobal.com](https://api.smsglobal.com)

`SoapApiUrl` = [https://api.smsglobal.com](https://api.smsglobal.com)

`AccountUsername` = \[your MXT Master API Key Username\]

`AccountPassword` = \[your MXT Master API Key Password\]

`RestApiKey` = \[your REST API Key\]

`RestApiSecret` = \[your REST API Secret\]

There are also 2 dynamic environment variables that are automatically set by pre/post request scripts.

`authorization` - This value is populated when using the REST API.

`SoapApiTicket` - This value is populated when using the SOAP API.

item.description:
SMSGlobal HTTP API .

Find your API credentials in the MXT dashboard: [https://mxt.smsglobal.com/integrations](https://mxt.smsglobal.com/integrations) and copy your Master API Key Username and Password.

On the Postman `Environments` tab, set the following environment variables:

`AccountUsername` = MXT Master API Key Username

`AccountPassword` = MXT Master API Key Password

`HttpApiUrl` = [https://api.smsglobal.com](https://api.smsglobal.com)

item.name: OTP
item.description:
SMSGlobal OTP API .

View the Documentation: [https://www.smsglobal.com/otp-api](https://www.smsglobal.com/otp-api/)

Find your REST/OTP API credentials in the MXT dashboard: [https://mxt.smsglobal.com/integrations](https://mxt.smsglobal.com/integrations) - Create a REST API Key/Secret for using this API.

On the Postman `Environments` tab, set the following environment variables:

`RestApiUrl` = [https://api.smsglobal.com](https://api.smsglobal.com)

`RestApiKey` = \[your REST API Key\]

`RestApiSecret` = \[your REST API Secret\]

The REST and OTP APIs also use a dynamic environment variable that is automatically set by pre/-request scripts.

`authorization` - This value is populated for authenticating requests - it also uses the above environment variables.

exec: var authHeader = 'MAC id="' + apiKey + '", ts="' + ts + '", nonce="' + nonce + '", mac="' + authHash + '"';

item.description:
SMSGlobal SOAP API .

View the Documentation: [https://www.smsglobal.com/soap-api/](https://www.smsglobal.com/soap-api/)

View the WSDL: [https://api.smsglobal.com/soap/soapserver.php?wsdl](https://api.smsglobal.com/soap/soapserver.php?wsdl)

Find your SOAP API credentials in the MXT dashboard: [https://mxt.smsglobal.com/integrations](https://mxt.smsglobal.com/integrations) and copy your Master API Key Username and Password.

On the Postman `Environments` tab, set the following environment variables:

`AccountUsername` = MXT Master API Key Username

`AccountPassword` = MXT Master API Key Password

`SoapApiUrl` = [https://api.smsglobal.com](https://api.smsglobal.com)

The SOAP API also uses a dynamic environment variable that is automatically set by post-response script.

`SoapApiToken` - This value is populated for authenticating requests - it also uses the above environment variables.

Start with the `apiValidateLogin` request to get your API token. A successful response from this request will return your SOAP API `ticket` and will be saved as the `SoapApiTicket` environment variable, which is subsequently used in all other SOAP API requests.
